headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while ETF desks keep buying and whales keep sending coins to exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unanimous: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. That's seven for seven. Bitcoin sits 49.0% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51 at $63,653.85, and the rest are worse: ADA is 83.2% off its high, DOGE 75.7%, SOL 70.4%. When the whole board agrees on a trend, you don't need much else to characterize the tape: this is a market working lower from a peak, not one grinding out fresh highs.

But momentum tells a more mixed story than trend does, and that gap is worth naming. BTC's RSI-14 is 47.4, roughly neutral, with MACD below signal, down 0.3% on the day, down 1.6% on the week, down 3.0% on the month: a clean, consistent slide across every window. ETH is the outlier on the board. It's down 0.8% on the day but up 1.8% on the week and up 6.4% on the month, RSI 56.3 (the highest of the group), even though price still sits below the 200-day and MACD is bearish. That's a coin catching a short-term bid inside a longer downtrend, a genuine divergence, not noise. XRP, BNB, and ADA all show similar day-versus-month splits (small daily gains or flat prints sitting on top of month-long losses of 5-12%), which means the recent calm is recent, not resolved.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. Funding is positive and modest across the board, from BTC's 6.9% annualized to XRP's 11.0%, meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade almost everywhere. That's a crowd still leaning long, but the long/short account ratios show where the real crowding is: XRP at 2.41 and DOGE at 3.62, both far more lopsided than BTC's 1.09. The liquidation tape over the last 24 hours confirms who's been wrong: BTC longs lost $11.7M against $1.6M in shorts, ETH longs lost $12.3M against $3.0M in shorts, roughly 7-to-1 and 4-to-1 skews. Crowded long, mildly expensive to hold, and already getting flushed on the margin. That's fragile positioning, not fuel.

Now the flows, and here's where the tape stops agreeing with itself. US spot ETFs printed a net $314.3M into BTC and $179.8M into ETH on 25 Aug 2026, both extending seven straight days in the same direction, with five-session totals of $2,082.9M and $885.7M respectively. That's real, sustained buying from the traditional-finance side. At the same time, whale wallets moved $169.9M net onto exchanges over the last 24 hours, almost entirely an ETH story ($170.2M onto exchanges) while BTC was roughly flat (a small $368,724 net off exchanges). Zoom out to the weekly pattern and it's been three straight weeks of net onto-exchange flow (week ending Aug 12: $998M, Aug 19: $220M, Aug 26: $1,289M), reversing the $1,225M that moved off exchanges in the week ending Aug 05. Coins moving toward exchanges is usually read as supply looking for a bid, and it's happening in the same window ETFs are absorbing supply. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat over 30 days (+0.34%) at $309.0B, so there's no meaningful build in sideline cash to explain either side of this.

Sentiment sits at 65, labeled Greed, inside a 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is feeling good in a market where every asset is below its long-term trend line and whales have been feeding exchanges for three consecutive weeks. That gap between mood and behavior is the read for today. Worth watching from here: whether the seven-day streak of ETF inflows holds or breaks, whether the weekly whale flow turns back toward off-exchange (as it did the week ending Aug 05), and whether ETH's RSI/price divergence resolves by price catching up to momentum or momentum fading back toward the group.
